card.title: Seoul Autumn Walk

items.find: Maple leaves turning brilliant crimson and gold on the branches.
items.why: As chlorophyll breaks down in autumn, other pigments like carotenoids become visible, providing bright colour.

items.find: Patches of moss clinging damply to shaded, rough tree bark.
items.why: Mosses thrive in moist, shaded environments, retaining moisture through dense, velvety leaf-like structures.

items.find: How many small, dark brown acorn caps are visible on the ground?
items.why: Acorns are the seeds of oak trees, designed to survive winter until germination conditions are right.

items.find: How many small, brownish birds are visible moving in the canopy?
items.why: These calls often serve as territorial warnings or communicate feeding locations to flock members.

items.find: A patch of ground covered in crunchy, dry leaf litter, rustling underfoot.
items.why: Decomposition of leaf litter is a vital process that returns nutrients to the soil for new growth.

card.sit_spot: Pause near a large, exposed root system and notice the texture of the earth around it for one full minute.
